decisions.evidence: In band1, line 6 (נֵבוֹשׁ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד :), two dots are stacked after וָעֶד, with a space before כִּי. The full page s110 shows the same thing. This is a sof-pasuq-style colon, not a single period.

This is the last word of band1 line 6. A dark dot sits inside the first bet, above its base stroke, and it is separate from the qamatz below. The full page agrees. Resolution is limited, but the interior mark is there on both images.
In band1 line 8, after לְאַרְצֵנוּ and before כִּי אֵל פּוֹעֵל, there are two stacked dots. The full page confirms them.

This is in band3 line 1. The marks under the vav and bet of וּבְשָׁכְבְּךָ run together at this resolution. I can't separate a meteg under the shuruq vav from the sheva and tipcha cluster. A crop of this word at native resolution is needed.

This is in band3 line 6 (after אֶת־יְהוָה). The hataf segol under the alef is clear, and so is the holam dot over the lamed. The pashta above the end of the word is also visible. A short vertical stroke under the lamed can't be confirmed or ruled out: it merges with the hataf segol cluster at this scale.

This is in band3 line 7. There seem to be marks below both וְנָתַתִּי and מְטַר besides the vowels: a vertical stroke near the qamatz of the nun, and a stroke near the patah of the tet. So the meteg might be on either word, on both, or one of the strokes might be a disjunctive accent. Nothing in the pixels at this resolution lets me assign the meteg to one host. Do not fill this from memory. Crop both words natively.
